about: Rules written down on a date. `node cli.js ledger` scores each one only on games played after its registration date: a rule found by searching old results can only be tested fairly on games that had not happened yet. Two kinds: a team's result rule (calendar / order), and league-wide picks against the point spread (type pick, from the lattice lab), scored as covers of the picked side. Add a rule by appending an entry with today's date.

rules.text: If Seattle's results 28 and 10 days before a game agree, predict that result again.
If Seattle's game is exactly 10 days after its previous game, and the previous and fourth-previous results agree, predict that result again.
More rest than the opponent should help; does the line price it fully? Back the side that is: 3+ more rest days than the opponent.
Teams off a bye against teams that were not. Back the side that is: off a bye (13+ days of rest) + opponent on 9 or fewer days of rest.
Thursday games give the visitor a short week and a trip. Back the side that is: home team + Thursday game.
A 1 pm Eastern kickoff is 10 am on a Pacific body clock. Fade the side that is: Pacific-time team + road team + game in the Eastern time zone + kickoff before 2 pm ET.

At a night kickoff a Pacific team is at its daily peak while an Eastern team is 3 hours later in its day (the circadian finding of Smith et al., 1997). Back the side that is: Pacific-time team + opponent is an Eastern-time team + night game (6:30 pm ET or later).
Road teams 2+ time zones from home. Fade the side that is: road team 2+ time zones from home.
The loser of the first meeting in a season, in the rematch. Back the side that is: lost to this opponent earlier this season.
After a 21+ point loss the market may overreact. Back the side that is: team lost its last game by 21+.
After a 21+ point win the market may overreact. Fade the side that is: team won its last game by 21+.
Teams that covered 3 straight: the line may chase them. Fade the side that is: team covered its last 3.
Teams that failed to cover 3 straight. Back the side that is: team failed to cover its last 3.
Division rivals know each other; underdogs may keep it closer. Back the side that is: division game + underdog.
Double-digit underdogs: the public backs favorites. Back the side that is: underdog by 10+.
In weeks 1-4 the line may lean too hard on last season. Back the side that is: weeks 1-4 + losing record last season.

Big favorites in night games draw public money. Fade the side that is: favored by 7-9.5 + night game (6:30 pm ET or later); or Fade the side that is: favored by 10+ + night game (6:30 pm ET or later).
Control: nothing should happen. Home teams within 1.5 days of a full moon. Back the side that is: home team + within 1.5 days of a full moon.

The hand-found 10-day / 4th-previous rule as a bet: after 10 days, back a team whose last and 4th-previous games were wins, fade one whose were losses. Back the side that is: last game exactly 10 days before + last and 4th-previous games both wins; or Fade the side that is: last game exactly 10 days before + last and 4th-previous games both losses.

The hand-found 28/10 rule as a bet: back a team that won the games 28 and 10 days before, fade one that lost both. Back the side that is: won the games 28 and 10 days before; or Fade the side that is: lost the games 28 and 10 days before.
Found by the machine search on 1999-2012 (rank 1). Back the side that is: Sunday game + team lost its last game + lost the last meeting with this opponent.
Found by the machine search on 1999-2012 (rank 2). Fade the side that is: Central-time team + opponent lost its last game + won the last meeting with this opponent.
Found by the machine search on 1999-2012 (rank 3). Fade the side that is: home team + division game + November game.
